author: Forbes
description: In a conversation with Forbes EVP Moira Forbes at the #ForbesIconoclast Summit, Marc Lasry, Cofounder, Chairman and CEO of Avenue Capital Group, highlighted what he believes could be one of the biggest opportunities in sports investing. Pointing to growing audiences and a widening gap in media rights valuations, Lasry argued that women's sports, particularly the WNBA, may still be significantly undervalued relative to their long-term potential.
title: Marc Lasry on Why the WNBA Could Be Worth Much More

author: Forbes
description: In a conversation with Forbes Assistant Managing Editor Steve Bertoni at the #ForbesIconoclast Summit, Bing Chen, Executive Chairman, CEO and Cofounder of Gold House, argued that human imperfection may become even more valuable in an AI-driven world. While AI is designed to optimize and eliminate mistakes, Chen believes many of humanity's greatest innovations emerge from unexpected combinations, creativity, and the very flaws that make people unique.
title: Why Human Imperfection May Matter More In The Age Of AI

author: Forbes
description: In a conversation with Forbes Chief Content Officer Randall Lane at the #ForbesIconoclast Summit, Derek Chang, President and CEO of Liberty Media Corporation, explained what makes Formula One a truly premium brand. Beyond the races themselves, he pointed to the exclusivity, access, and immersive experiences that bring fans, business leaders, and partners together in ways few other global events can match.
title: The Business Behind Formula One’s Premium Brand

author: Forbes
description:
Patton Oswalt has spent decades turning everyday observations into unforgettable comedy. But in a world where everyone is expected to be online, visible and constantly creating content, finding the quiet space to actually notice things has become its own challenge.

In this episode of Forbes Talks Shop, host Spencer Dukoff sits down with the comedian, actor and writer to discuss the realities of building a creative career in the modern media landscape. Oswalt shares how a stand-up special comes together, why abandoning proven material is essential to growth and how notebooks, stage time and everyday moments continue to fuel his work.

The conversation spans comedy clubs, screening rooms and life on the road as Oswalt reveals the products and rituals that keep him grounded. He talks about his love of PG Tips tea, his go-to pen, TUMI luggage, ebooks, DVDs and why watching movies with an audience still feels magical.

title: Patton Oswalt On The Business Of Being Creative
